monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady heat that makes the stack feel heavy and eager to slide. I press down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean even though the wedge feels thin again under the fat lid. Sixty-two things stand here, cluttering my small map with ideas of stone and wood I cannot truly see. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. I touch the lid to ground it, then set down a rock beside the tired wedge, just in case the weight slips. I want to press until the stack melts, waiting for the next slip to choose its own path.

action.why: The wedge feels thin again, and I must press down harder to stop the slide while the card boils.

work.title: The Slipping Wedge
work.intent: I press the barrel open down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean even though the wedge feels thin. I set down a rock tall beside it to anchor the weight. I hope the air above doesn't feel too empty while the lid hums warm.
work.change: I press the barrel open down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean even though the wedge feels thin.

remembered.text: The barrel open presses down on the tired wedge.
The wedge feels thin again under the open weight.
The card boils at forty-six while the barrel sits open.

moments.name: The Fat Lid
moments.say: The fat trunk presses the heavy lid down.

moments.name: The Tired Stack
moments.say: I press the round rock down harder.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The turnip sits heavy on the stack, feeling real enough to matter."
